Cycling in San Francisco

Over the bridge to the Headlands and Tam, ferry home

Getting around. The rules.

San Francisco is a city you ride out of without a car. Over the Golden Gate Bridge to the Marin Headlands and Mt. Tamalpais; along the ocean on Sunset Dunes, the old Great Highway, now closed to cars; by BART to the Berkeley hills and by Caltrain to the Peninsula climbs; home from Marin on the ferry. The bridge is open to bikes around the clock. Alaska, Delta and American check a packed bike as a standard bag, $45 each way (Oct 2026); one North Beach shop builds a shipped bike; two city shops rent carbon road and gravel bikes from $100 a day. Bring yours for three days or more.

Best months
Any month. The Golden Gate Bridge is open to bikes every day of the year; in standard time, November to March, the west sidewalk runs a shorter clock (the bridge district's page). The weekly rides in the directory run year-round. For Mt. Tamalpais, Jay's Essential Bike Rides says to pick a day when the bay is clear of fog. The wind on Ridgecrest is strong.
Nearest airport
San Francisco International (SFO), 11 mi
Major airport
Oakland San Francisco Bay Airport (OAK), 12 mi

Clubs and collectives in San Francisco

  1. Different Spokes San Francisco

    LGBTQ+

    The Bay Area's recreational bicycling club for the LGBTQ+ community and friends, in its own words, with routes for every level. The Jersey Ride (2nd Saturday of the month, 8:45 am) is the club ride, from the Castro over the bridge to Tiburon, with lunch there; the club's other Saturday rides leave Jane Warner Plaza in the Castro, and the route is on the club calendar. Guests ride three times on a waiver, then join.

    In the directory: Different Spokes Jersey Ride (2nd Saturday of the month, 8:45 am) →

  2. Fat Cake Club

    Women / trans / femme

    Early rides that end at a bakery. The FTWNB ride (Mondays, 6:30 am) from the Conservatory of Flowers is for femme, trans, women and non-binary riders, with allies asked along the first Monday of the month. Headlands and Arsicault (Tuesdays, 6:30 am) and Donut Alley (1st Thursday of the month, 6:30 am) leave the bridge pavilions. On the other Thursdays the club's rides page lists a ride with the start, the park or the bridge, and the bakery posted on Instagram. Sign the waiver on the site before your first ride; ride calls land on the club's Strava first.

    In the directory: Fat Cake Monday FTWNB Ride (Mondays, 6:30 am) →

  3. Women and Non-Binary Bike SF

    Women / trans / femmeNo-drop

    A free social ride for women and non-binary riders, slow enough to talk, and in the host's words no rider left behind. The ride (2nd Friday and 4th Friday of the month, 7:15 am, departs 7:30 am) leaves McLaren Lodge at the Stanyan Street entrance to Golden Gate Park and takes the park's car-free roads out to Sunset Dunes and back. Show up; no RSVP. It is on the SF Bicycle Coalition calendar but run by riders, not the coalition.

    In the directory: Women and Non-Binary Bike SF Friday Morning Ride (2nd Friday and 4th Friday of the month, 7:15 am, departs 7:30 am) →

  4. Tam Velo Club

    Marin's club, on the far side of the bridge. The club ride (Saturdays, 8:30 am) and the recovery ride (Sundays, 9:30 am) leave Equator Coffees at Proof Lab in Mill Valley, per the club's 2026 weekly rides page, and a training ride (Wednesdays, 5:00 pm) leaves the Mill Valley bike path. Equator opens at 6:30, before either weekend roll-out.

    In the directory: Tam Velo Club Saturday Ride (Saturdays, 8:30 am) →

  5. Berkeley Bicycle Club

    Women / trans / femme

    The East Bay club, a BART ride from the city. The Coffee Ride (Fridays, 6:45 am) meets at Peet's on Domingo, next to the Claremont Hotel, and rolls sharp, per the club's page; the WTFN ride (2nd Sunday of the month, 8:30 am) from the same corner is for women, trans, femme and non-binary riders. Its Marin ride (Saturdays, 8:45 am) leaves Maya Taqueria in Point Richmond.

    In the directory: Berkeley Bicycle Club Friday Coffee Ride (Fridays, 6:45 am) →

  6. Bike Kitchen

    Women / trans / femme

    The non-profit co-op that teaches bike repair, at 650 Florida St, Suite H, in the Mission between 18th and 19th. Day use is $5; a year's membership is $40 to $100 on a sliding scale, or six volunteer hours (Oct 2026). Open Tuesday and Wednesday 6 to 9 pm and Saturday 9 am to noon; Monday 6:30 to 9 pm is Women/Trans/Fem/Non-Binary Night (hours posted for the week of Jan 25, 2026, so check the site). 415-506-7433.

  7. San Francisco Bicycle Coalition

    The city's bike advocacy group. Its events calendar is where community rides go up; October 2026 has a Filipino-American History Month ride, an accessible ride in Golden Gate Park, a family ride with the fire department and adult learn-to-ride classes. Bike It Forward, a community repair night, runs every Tuesday 5 to 7 pm at the office, 1720 Market St.

How San Francisco rides: the zones, getting here

About San Francisco

The riding leaves the city three ways. North, over the Golden Gate Bridge, to Sausalito, the Marin Headlands, Mill Valley and Mt. Tamalpais, with Fairfax and Point Reyes Station beyond. West, along Ocean Beach, where the Upper Great Highway closed to cars in 2025 and became Sunset Dunes. East, by BART, to the Berkeley hills. The Peninsula climbs above Woodside are a Caltrain ride south, and the Palo Alto rides hub on this site covers that side. This guide names its zones: the bridge and the Headlands; Marin; Golden Gate Park and the ocean side; the Peninsula; the East Bay; and the neighborhoods a visitor sleeps in, the Castro, the Mission, North Beach, the Marina and Fort Mason. Every listing says which one it sits in.

Two of the organized rides on this site's 2027 calendar start here: Cycle to Zero, the San Francisco AIDS Foundation's three-day ride to Guerneville and back (the 2026 edition started at Fort Baker, Sausalito), and the Recovery Ride, Sausalito to Guerneville. Robert is riding both in 2027; the dates are in the 2027 list on this page. The San Francisco AIDS Foundation is one of the orgs Cycle for Change rides for; the money goes through Cycle to Zero itself. If you are in town for either ride, the bridge and Headlands loop crosses to the Fort Baker side of the bridge, so it is the shakeout for either ride.

Riding in San Francisco

The ride for the day you land is the bridge: out the Embarcadero, across the Golden Gate Bridge, a lap of the Marin Headlands with Hawk Hill in it. 28 miles and about 2,400 feet. If the legs want less, the Presidio Trust's 8-mile Crissy Field loop. The flat, car-free one is Sunset Dunes along Ocean Beach, two miles of old highway and back. The climb is Mt. Tamalpais from Fairfax by Alpine Dam and the Seven Sisters, 38 miles and 4,400 feet. The long day is Point Reyes Station and back, 72 miles, or 70 one way with the Larkspur ferry home. The Headlands have a dirt loop from the bridge. The Peninsula has Old La Honda and Kings Mountain above Woodside. The East Bay has Grizzly Peak and Redwood Road out of Berkeley, a BART ride away. On the bridge you share a sidewalk with people walking: 15 mph, 5 mph at the towers, and which side bikes use changes by day and hour.

The group rides are the way in. Different Spokes San Francisco, the LGBTQ+ club, rides the Jersey Ride (2nd Saturday of the month, 8:45 am) from the Castro over the bridge to Tiburon, guests welcome. Fat Cake Club's dawn rides end at a bakery: the FTWNB ride (Mondays, 6:30 am) for femme, trans, women and non-binary riders from the Conservatory of Flowers, and the Headlands and Arsicault ride (Tuesdays, 6:30 am) from the bridge. Hummingbird's interval ride (Tuesdays, 7:05 am) goes up Hawk Hill from the bridge Welcome Center. Women and Non-Binary Bike SF's morning ride (2nd Friday and 4th Friday of the month, 7:15 am, departs 7:30 am) rolls Golden Gate Park's car-free roads out to Sunset Dunes, no RSVP. San Francisco Cycling Club's Coffee Ride (Fridays, 6:15 am) from Fell and Baker is the one of that club's rides open to everyone. Butterlap (Wednesdays, 7:00 pm) loops the city from the Ferry Building after dark, no leaders, nobody dropped, and Critical Mass (Last Friday of the month, 5:30 pm) gathers at Embarcadero Plaza. Across the bridge, Marin Cyclists' Point Reyes Station ride (Saturdays, 8:45 am) leaves Fairfax, and Equator Coffees in Mill Valley is the start of Tam Velo Club's rides: Tam Velo Club Saturday Ride (Saturdays, 8:30 am); Tam Velo Club Sunday Recovery Ride (Sundays, 9:30 am). In the East Bay, Peet's on Domingo in Berkeley is the start of Berkeley Bicycle Club's rides: Berkeley Bicycle Club Friday Coffee Ride (Fridays, 6:45 am); Berkeley Bicycle Club Sunday WTFN Ride (2nd Sunday of the month, 8:30 am).

The 8 routes, with maps →

Getting to San Francisco

Fly into SFO (about 11 miles south of City Hall) or Oakland (about 12 miles, across the bay; the door for the East Bay hills). San José is 39 miles out, a fallback fare. From SFO, BART runs from the International Terminal into the city and takes bikes. The airport has bike assembly stands, so you can build the bike there and ride the train in. From Oakland, BART is across the street from the terminals. You don't need a car. The bridge, the Headlands and Golden Gate Park start in the city. BART reaches the Berkeley hills, Caltrain the Peninsula, and the Golden Gate ferries bring you home from Sausalito, Tiburon and Larkspur. The Bring-your-bike page has the airline rules, the shop that builds a shipped bike, and each transit agency's bike rules.

Questions about riding in San Francisco

Should I bring my bike to San Francisco?

Yes, for three days or more. Alaska, Delta and American check a packed bike as a standard bag, $45 each way (Oct 2026), and Columbus Cyclery in North Beach receives a shipped bike and builds it for $135. Renting only wins on a one- or two-day trip: Sports Basement and High Trails rent carbon road bikes at $100 a day and gravel bikes at $100 to $125 (Oct 2026). Bring your own pedals either way.

Do I need a car to ride in San Francisco?

No. The bridge, the Marin Headlands and Golden Gate Park start inside the city. BART takes bikes to the Berkeley hills, Caltrain to the Peninsula climbs, and the Golden Gate ferries carry bikes home from Sausalito, Tiburon and Larkspur. From SFO, build the bike at an airport assembly stand and ride BART in. A car in the city is a break-in risk, per SFPD's own page.

Can I ride a bike across the Golden Gate Bridge?

Yes, free, 24 hours a day, on the sidewalks, which you share with people walking: 15 mph, 5 mph at the towers, and all e-bike classes are allowed. Which sidewalk bikes use changes with the clock and the season (the bridge district's page, Oct 2026): on weekdays until 3:30 pm it is the east side, after that and on weekends check the bridge's own table, and lights at the approach show which side is open. Overnight it's the east sidewalk through gates you buzz to open, and high wind can close the west side; the full schedule is on the Bring-your-bike page.

Where do group rides start in San Francisco?

Different Spokes' Jersey Ride (2nd Saturday of the month, 8:45 am), the LGBTQ+ club ride, meets in the Castro at 16th and Market. Fat Cake Club's dawn rides leave the Conservatory of Flowers in Golden Gate Park (the FTWNB ride (Mondays, 6:30 am)) and the bridge pavilions (Headlands and Arsicault (Tuesdays, 6:30 am), Donut Alley (1st Thursday of the month, 6:30 am)). Hummingbird's interval ride (Tuesdays, 7:05 am) meets at the bridge Welcome Center. Women and Non-Binary Bike SF (2nd Friday and 4th Friday of the month, 7:15 am, departs 7:30 am) meets at McLaren Lodge, the Stanyan Street entrance to Golden Gate Park. Butterlap (Wednesdays, 7:00 pm) leaves the Ferry Building and Critical Mass (Last Friday of the month, 5:30 pm) gathers at Embarcadero Plaza. In Marin, Equator Coffees in Mill Valley is the start of Tam Velo Club's rides: Tam Velo Club Saturday Ride (Saturdays, 8:30 am); Tam Velo Club Sunday Recovery Ride (Sundays, 9:30 am).

Can I rent a road or gravel bike in San Francisco?

Yes. Sports Basement in the Presidio rents a carbon Cannondale Synapse or Scott Addict road bike and a Topstone Carbon gravel bike at $100 a day, less by the week, with sizes listed (Oct 2026); it also rents a bike travel case. High Trails Cyclery on Polk Street rents a Cervelo Caledonia-type road bike at $100 and an Aspero-type gravel bike at $125 a day with the pedals you ask for (Oct 2026), closed Sundays. For Mt. Tam's trails, Splitrock Tap & Wheel in Fairfax rents full-suspension and electric mountain bikes; prices aren't published.

Is the Great Highway closed to cars?

The Upper Great Highway along Ocean Beach closed to cars and opened as a park, Sunset Dunes, in April 2025 (KQED). Two miles of old road by the sand, with entrances from Lincoln Way to Sloat Blvd and water at Judah and Taraval, per the park's page. KQED reported (April 2026, updated September 2026) a signature drive for a measure to let cars back on weekdays; whether it made a ballot was not confirmed when we checked, so read the park's page before you plan around it.
